title: Automated Error-Budget Salvage and Safeguard Runbook
author: Priya K. Rao
body:
Summary:
This runbook defines the automated "salvage" sequence Redwood uses when an SLO is at risk of breach due to sudden demand or cascading failures. It documents precise trigger thresholds, automated actions the Error-Budget Controller (EBC) performs, verification steps, and escalation criteria for human intervention. The goal is to preserve customer-visible SLOs while minimizing cost and avoiding risky manual changes during short-lived incidents.

Scope:
- Applies to platform-facing services that contribute directly to customer-facing SLOs: inference-gateway, request-router, kv-cache-service, batch-assembler, model-allocator, and autoscaler.
- Covers both Hosted API and Dedicated deployments where EBC is active.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance windows and long-running degradations (>72h) which require runbook escalation to Service Owners.

Key definitions:
- SLO Window: 30-day rolling window for availability and p95 latency.
- Error Budget: 1 - SLO (e.g., for a 99.9% availability SLO, error budget = 0.1%).
- Salvage Window: 30 minutes from first threshold crossing.
- EBC (Error-Budget Controller): automated component that evaluates telemetry and issues policy actions.

High-level policy & thresholds:
1) Watcher thresholds (continuous):
   - Watcher-Alert (early): projected error budget burn rate > 5x for next 24 hours (based on last 15-minute trend).
   - Salvage-Trigger (automatic): projected error budget burn rate > 15x and projected remaining budget < 6 hours.
   - Critical-Escalate: projected remaining budget < 1 hour OR sudden p95 spike > 3x baseline

2) Priority ordering for automated remediation (executed by EBC):
   - Level A (fast, reversible, low-risk): enable cross-region routing to standby region for low-latency tenants, temporarily relax tenant-specific throttles by 10% for Class B tenants, activate short-lived balloon capacity (burst GPUs) with auto-expire 45m.
   - Level B (moderate risk/cost): force-prefix-cache warm (pre-warm KV entries for hot prefixes), increase batch size heuristics for background non-interactive requests up to safe limit, open read-only fallback for non-critical model variants.
   - Level C (higher cost/impact): spin up additional model-allocator pools (quantized model variants), preempt lower-priority background jobs and throttled training tasks, switch to higher-cost low-latency instance types for the next 30 minutes.

Automated Salvage Sequence (step-by-step):
1) Detection & Validation (0–90s):
   - EBC detects Salvage-Trigger via SLO prediction job (15s cadence).
   - Validate signal: cross-check with telemetry pipeline (prometheus, traces) and synthetic canaries. Must see at least 2 corroborating signals (latency, error-rate or canary fail).
   - If validation fails, EBC records anomaly and re-checks at 30s, abort salvage if signals subside.

2) Pre-emptive Announcement (90–120s):
   - Post internal incident note to #sre-ops channel with automated summary: affected SLO, projected remaining budget, actions planned.
   - Create ephemeral incident in Incident Manager with severity=warning so SREs are aware.

3) Level A actions (120–300s):
   - Command: redwoodctl ebc action enable-cross-region --from=us-west-2 --to=us-east-1 --tenants=all-low-latency
   - Command: redwoodctl throttle relax --tenant-selection=classB --percent=10 --duration=45m
   - Command: redwoodctl capacity balloon --pool=inference-burst --size=gpu-t4x8 --duration=45m
   - After each action, EBC waits 30s, then asserts service-level telemetry improved (p95 reduced or error rate declined).

4) Level B actions (if Level A insufficient, 5–15m):
   - Pre-warm KV cache: redwoodctl kv prewarm --prefixes=@hotlist --parallel=8
   - Tune batching: redwoodctl runtime set-batching --service=request-router --batch-size=adaptive --max-inflight=512
   - Promote read-only fallbacks for non-critical model variants: redwoodctl model promote-fallback --service=kv-cache-service --variants=ro-quantv1

5) Level C actions (if still insufficient, escalate and execute with approvals):
   - Spin up quantized allocator pools: redwoodctl allocator create --type=quant-8bit --count=4
   - Evict non-critical workloads: redwoodctl schedule evict --workload=training-jobs --grace=60s
   - Notify Finance/Capacity-owners for approval if estimated cost delta > $5000 in 24h.

Telemetry & Safety checks (always run):
- After each automated action the EBC uses these checks before proceeding further:
  * Canary verification: 3 sequential canary requests succeed for each critical path (generation, embedding).
  * Latency regression guard: no more than 10% p95 increase for unaffected tenants in 5m window.
  * Error amplification guard: if system error-rate doubles post-action, EBC rolls back the last action immediately.

Fast rollback rules (automated):
- Any Level A or B action that does not produce measurable improvement within 3 minutes is rolled back automatically.
- Any action causing collateral regressions (latency regressions for unaffected tenants or >1.5x increase in internal error events) is rolled back immediately.

Manual escalation criteria (immediately page rotating SRE):
- EBC cannot restore projected error budget burn below 5x within 20 minutes of Salvage-Trigger.
- Projected remaining budget drops below 1 hour at any point.
- Automated rollbacks occur more than 2 times for the same sequence within 30 minutes.

On-call checklist for SRE who takes ownership:
1) Acknowledge incident in Incident Manager and set severity based on projected remaining budget.
2) Review EBC action log (redwoodctl ebc show --incident-id=<id>) and the timeline of telemetry.
3) If Level C actions required, coordinate with Product & Capacity team and document approval in incident.
4) If root cause appears unrelated to capacity (e.g., infra networking or model corruption), switch to debugging checklist in "Forensic playbook: service-level causation" (see related pages).

Configuration examples (EBC policy snippet):

{
  "policy_name": "salvage-policy-default",
  "slo_window_days": "30",
  "watcher_threshold_factor": "5",
  "salvage_trigger_factor": "15",
  "salvage_window_minutes": "30",
  "level_a": "enable-cross-region,relax-throttles,balloon-capacity",
  "level_b": "prewarm-cache,adjust-batching,promote-readonly",
  "level_c": "create-quant-pools,evict-background,raise-instance-class"
}

Note: the internal EBC policy is stored in YAML in the config repo. Example YAML fragment stored at: configs/ebc/salvage/policy-default.yaml

Operational run commands (quick reference):
- View current EBC state: redwoodctl ebc status --service=inference-gateway
- Show recent actions: redwoodctl ebc actions --since=1h --json
- Force a sandboxed salvage (test mode): redwoodctl ebc action --simulate --policy=salvage-policy-default
- Rollback last EBC action: redwoodctl ebc rollback --action-id=<id>

Ownership & responsibilities:
- Primary owner: SRE Platform (on-call rotation).
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime (for runtime/batching changes).
- Alerting & Telemetry: Observability team maintains Prometheus rules and canary tests used by EBC.
- Cost approvals: Capacity Finance liaison (on-call list in Capacity playbook).

Post-incident workflow (after salvage concluded):
1) Incident triage meeting within 24 hours (required if error budget usage exceeded > 20% of monthly budget).
2) Artifact collection: EBC logs, promql queries, canary traces, redwoodctl action history.
3) Root-cause analysis (assign to owner) and proposed mitigations (capacity changes, runtime fixes, model variant rollouts).
4) Update the EBC policy if runbook actions caused collateral risk or were ineffective.

Runbook test exercises (recommended cadence):
- Monthly simulated salvage drills using redwoodctl ebc --simulate with injected telemetry patterns.
- Quarterly cross-team tabletop to validate approval flows for Level C actions.

Related pages & references:
- SLO oncall escalation and capacity triggers (operational reference)
- Error budget orchestration and traffic throttle playbook
- Forensic playbook: service-level causation and replay guidance
- configs/ebc/salvage/policy-default.yaml (config repo)

Appendix: quick SLO thresholds (for reference)
| Service             | SLO (p95 latency) | Error budget (30d) | Salvage-Trigger (projected) |
|---------------------|-------------------:|--------------------:|-----------------------------:|
| inference-gateway    | 250ms             | 0.1%               | <6 hours remaining           |
| request-router      | 120ms             | 0.2%               | <8 hours remaining           |
| kv-cache-service    | 30ms              | 0.05%              | <4 hours remaining           |

Change log:
- 2025-11-12: Initial draft by Priya K. Rao.
- 2025-12-04: Added Level B actions and pre-warm cache commands (reviewer feedback).
- 2026-02-03: Hardened rollback rules and added cost approval threshold.

Footer:
For questions or to propose a policy change, contact SRE Platform lead (sre-platform@redwood.com) and open a PR against configs/ebc/salvage/policy-default.yaml.
